correctness.rationale: The claim follows from the published Type-A iff characterization plus a bijective count. For each edge, the first and last differing coordinates give a unique interval; the Type-A theorem forces the two restrictions to be opposite alternating phases over one unordered symbol pair and forces equality outside. Conversely every such choice creates exactly two common deletion descendants. For interval length \(L\), the number of edges is \((n-L+1)q^{n-L}\binom{q}{2}\), and the finite geometric derivative identity gives the closed form. An independent stdlib verifier reconstructs deletion balls and the canonical alternating condition and checks their equivalence on 20 finite parameter pairs, including all binary blocklengths through \(9\). Finite verification is explicitly not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The forbidden-pair graph is the exact combinatorial object underlying two-read single-deletion reconstruction codes. Its total collision count and average degree are natural global invariants, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The formula holds for every alphabet size and blocklength, exposes a unique alternating-interval parametrization of every collision, and gives the asymptotic mean conflict degree \(n-q/(q-1)+o(1)\). It complements independence-number/code-size questions with exact graph density useful for structural bounds, probabilistic estimates, and finite benchmarks.
